main_text.head: ENCOMIASTICON.
main_text.p: Cœlesti ô utinam sit mens afflata furore, Et possim Magno concaluisse Deo! Concaluisse Deo, qui jussit datere Mosen Isacidas Rubrum per mare. Prodigium! Prodigium Pharío tortis immanius hydris! In muri speciem lympha marina stetit; Munit iter, Jadae tuto transfire potestas Quò sit; vexantes Nilicolasque necet. Concaluisse Deo, qui certo tempore Gnatum Misit ut orcino nos Pharaone levet. Concaluisse Deo, qui solvens ora Prophetis Hoc populum Vates praemonuisse dedit: Ut canerem laetus laudes & facta Jehovae, Cumque SALUTIFERI{a} ô FLAMEN, ubique tuas? Ut canerem Vatum praesagia; quique revelant, Quos inter lucet TILLIUS arte cata. Ille dedit Prodromum{b}, Matthaeum, Musica{c}, Psalmos; Illius hinc volitat fama per ora virum. Scilicet apparet doctus simul atque disertus: Lector infescatus non satiandus erat,

page.notes: Decorative woodcut initial C joined to "œlesti". Line "ô utinam" and the "ô" after SALUTIFERI are doubtful, possibly "ô" or "O". "Pharío" is doubtful. "datere" is doubtful, possibly "dare". "Jadae" is doubtful, possibly "Iadae" (read as Jadae). "infescatus" is doubtful. Italic/roman distinctions in the verse are approximate. The *** ornament between the text and the catchword is not transcribed. No page number, running head or signature is printed. Verse is given as one paragraph; the line breaks are not kept.
